title: French A1 · Week 1
description: French A1 Week 1: eight present-tense -ER priority verbs, 20 everyday nouns, daily active recall and speaking, Day 5 consolidation, Day 6 diagnostic revision, Day 7 articles/gender/plural and final assessment.

days.title: Parler & travailler
days.focus: Say what you speak and where you work
days.explanation:
DAY 1 — SIMPLE NOTES: PARLER & TRAVAILLER

1. MAKE A FRENCH SENTENCE
Start with WHO, then the ACTION, then the extra information.
WHO + VERB + REST.
Example: Je + parle + français. → Je parle français. (I speak French.)

2. LEARN THE TWO VERBS
parler = to speak; travailler = to work. They are regular -ER verbs.
To change a regular -ER verb, remove -er, then add the ending for the person:
je → -e (je parle) | tu → -es (tu parles) | il/elle → -e (elle parle)
nous → -ons (nous parlons) | vous → -ez (vous parlez) | ils/elles → -ent (ils parlent)
Important: The -ent in ils parlent is silent. Follow the conjugation tables above.

3. SMALL WORDS BEFORE NOUNS
A noun names a thing or place. Learn its article together with it:
la maison (house), l’appartement (apartment), la chambre (bedroom), le salon (living room), la cuisine (kitchen).
For now, remember each pair. We will explain article rules carefully on Day 7.

4. USEFUL EVERYDAY SENTENCES
Je parle français. = I speak French.
Je travaille à la maison. = I work at home.
Nous travaillons à la maison. = We work at home.

5. AVOID THESE MISTAKES
NOT « Je suis parle français. » → Say « Je parle français. »
NOT « Tu parle. » → Say « Tu parles. »
NOT « le maison » → Say « la maison ».

6. TRY FROM MEMORY
Without looking at the conjugation table, say: “We speak French.” → Nous parlons français.
Then hide these notes and do the exercises.
fixed: Je parle français. — I speak French.
Je travaille à la maison. — I work at home.

recall.explanation: Maison is a feminine noun: la maison. Learn the article with the noun.
Appartement is masculine, but le becomes l’ before a vowel: l’appartement.
Chambre is feminine: la chambre, not le chambre.
Salon is masculine: le salon.
Cuisine is feminine: la cuisine.
Être in the present: je suis; do not use je es.
Avoir in the present: j’ai. Je contracts to j’ before a vowel.

drills.explanation: Parler is regular -ER: je takes -e → je parle.
Travailler is regular -ER: nous takes -ons → nous travaillons.
With tu, a regular -ER verb takes -es → tu parles.
With elle, a regular -ER verb takes -e → elle travaille.
With ils, a regular -ER verb ends -ent, normally silent → ils parlent.

sentences.explanation: Say Je parle français. Do not add suis or de before français here.
Nous requires -ons: travaillons. At home is à la maison.
Elle uses -e, not -es or -ent: elle parle.

changes.prompt: Je parle français. → Change je to nous.
changes.explanation: Change both the subject and ending: je parle → nous parlons.

changes.prompt: Il travaille à la maison. → Change il to elles.
changes.explanation: Elles is plural; travailler ends -ent: elles travaillent.

oral: Oui, je travaille à la maison.
Et ton ami, il parle français ?
Say in French (without reading): I speak French.
Say in French: We work at home.
Say in French: They speak French.
exit: Write a NEW sentence using parler.
Ils parlent français.
Write a NEW sentence using travailler.
Elle travaille à la maison.

days.title: Habiter & aimer
days.focus: Say where you live and what you like
days.explanation:
DAY 2 — SIMPLE NOTES: HABITER & AIMER

1. REMEMBER YESTERDAY
parler = to speak; travailler = to work. With nous, add -ons: nous parlons, nous travaillons.

2. TODAY'S TWO VERBS
habiter = to live; aimer = to like. They use the same -ER endings as parler.
Examples: tu habites (you live), nous habitons (we live), elle aime (she likes), vous aimez (you like).

3. WHY DO WE WRITE J’ ?
If the next word starts with a vowel sound, je usually becomes j’.
je + aime → j’aime (I like)
je + habite → j’habite (I live). The h in habiter is silent.
NOT « je aime » or « je habite ». The apostrophe is important.

4. TWO READY-TO-USE PATTERNS
J’habite dans un appartement. = I live in an apartment.
J’habite dans une maison. = I live in a house.
J’aime le salon. = I like the living room.
Use aimer + le/la/les when saying what you like in general: J’aime la cuisine.

5. TODAY'S FIVE NOUNS
la table (table), la chaise (chair), la fenêtre (window), le lit (bed), la porte (door).
Say a full sentence: La table est dans la cuisine. / Le lit est dans la chambre.
Learn each noun with its article: NOT « le chaise »; say « la chaise ».

6. TRY FROM MEMORY
Say in French: “I live in an apartment.” → J’habite dans un appartement.
Then change I to we: Nous habitons dans un appartement.
Hide the notes before your written and speaking practice.
fixed: J’habite dans un appartement. — I live in an apartment.
J’aime la chambre. — I like the bedroom.

recall.explanation: Table is feminine, so la table.
Chaise is feminine, so la chaise.
Fenêtre is feminine and keeps its accent: la fenêtre.
Lit is masculine, so le lit.
Porte is feminine, so la porte.
Cuisine from Day 1 is feminine: la cuisine.
Parler with nous takes -ons: nous parlons.

drills.explanation: Because habiter begins with a silent h, je becomes j’: j’habite.
Aimer with tu takes -es: tu aimes.
Aimer with nous takes -ons: nous aimons.
Habiter with elles takes -ent: elles habitent.
Recall yesterday’s -ER ending: il travaille, not il travaillent.

sentences.explanation: J’habite uses elision; dans un appartement is the taught chunk.
Aimer with elle takes -e; cuisine is feminine: la cuisine.
Nous aimons ends -ons, and la maison is feminine.

changes.prompt: J’habite dans une maison. → Change je to ils.
changes.explanation: Je → ils changes j’habite to ils habitent; une maison stays feminine.

changes.prompt: Tu aimes la chambre. → Change tu to vous.
changes.explanation: Tu → vous changes tu aimes to vous aimez (-ez).

oral: Tu habites dans une maison ou dans un appartement ?
Say in French: I live in an apartment.
Say in French: She likes the kitchen.
Say in French, recalling Day 1: We speak French.
exit: Write a NEW sentence using habiter.
Nous habitons dans une maison.
Write a NEW sentence using aimer.
Elle aime le salon.
days.yesterday: Review Day 1: parler and travailler, plus la maison and la cuisine.

days.title: Chercher & demander
days.focus: Look for everyday items and request them
days.explanation:
DAY 3 — SIMPLE NOTES: CHERCHER & DEMANDER

1. QUICK REVIEW
J’habite = I live; j’aime = I like. We write j’ because these verbs begin with a vowel sound.

2. TWO NEW ACTION WORDS
chercher = to look for something.
demander = to ask for or request something.
Both are regular -ER verbs: je cherche, tu cherches, nous cherchons; elle demande, vous demandez.

3. EASY SENTENCE PATTERNS
Je cherche + the thing. → Je cherche le pain. (I am looking for the bread.)
Elle demande + the thing. → Elle demande une chaise. (She asks for a chair.)
Do NOT add pour after chercher here: « Je cherche le pain », not « Je cherche pour le pain ».
In this lesson, le pain and le lait refer to particular items you are looking for. A different way to ask for an unspecified amount of food comes later.

4. TODAY'S FIVE NOUNS
le pain (bread), le lait (milk), les œufs (eggs), l’épicerie (grocery store), le supermarché (supermarket).
Remember: les shows plural here (eggs); l’ appears before the first vowel sound in épicerie.
Examples: Tu cherches les œufs. / Nous cherchons le supermarché.

5. WATCH THESE MISTAKES
NOT « Nous demande. » → Nous demandons. (nous needs -ons)
NOT « le épicerie » → l’épicerie.
NOT « une chaise » with le → chaise is feminine: une chaise / la chaise.

6. TRY FROM MEMORY
Say: “She asks for a chair.” → Elle demande une chaise.
Say: “We are looking for the milk.” → Nous cherchons le lait.
Hide these notes and try the tasks without help.
fixed: Je cherche le pain. — I am looking for bread.
Je demande un livre. — I ask for a book.

recall.explanation: Pain is masculine: le pain.
Lait is masculine: le lait.
Œufs is plural: les œufs; keep œ (or oe on keyboards only if teacher allows).
Épicerie is feminine; la becomes l’ before the vowel é.
Supermarché is masculine: le supermarché; keep the final accent.
Chaise is feminine: la chaise (Day 2).
Elle + aimer takes -e: elle aime (Day 2).

drills.explanation: Regular -ER: je cherche (-e). Never insert pour after chercher for a direct object.
Regular -ER: nous demandons (-ons).
Regular -ER: tu demandes (-es).
Regular -ER: elles cherchent (-ent, usually silent).
Recall aimer: il aime (-e).

sentences.prompt: I am looking for the bread (specific bread).
sentences.explanation: Je cherche le pain means you are looking for the specific bread; no pour.
Elle demande une chaise; chaise is feminine, so une.

sentences.prompt: We are looking for the milk (specific milk).
sentences.explanation: Nous cherchons le lait; nous needs -ons and lait is masculine.

changes.prompt: Tu cherches les œufs. → Change tu to nous.
changes.explanation: Tu cherches → nous cherchons; les œufs remains plural.

changes.prompt: Elle demande un livre. → Change elle to ils.
changes.explanation: Elle demande → ils demandent; un livre stays singular.

oral: Tu cherches le pain ou le lait ?
Tu demandes un livre ou une chaise ?
Say in French: She asks for a chair.
Say in French: We are looking for the milk.
Say in French, recalling Day 2: I like the house.
exit: Write a NEW sentence using chercher.
Elle cherche le lait.
Write a NEW sentence using demander.
Nous demandons une chaise.

days.title: Regarder & écouter
days.focus: Talk about watching and listening, and reuse food vocabulary
days.explanation:
DAY 4 — SIMPLE NOTES: REGARDER & ÉCOUTER

1. REMEMBER AN OLD VERB
chercher = to look for; demander = to request. You already know their -ER endings.

2. TWO NEW VERBS
regarder = to watch or look at.
écouter = to listen to.
Examples: je regarde, tu regardes, nous regardons; j’écoute, vous écoutez, elles écoutent.
Remember: je + écoute → j’écoute. Keep the accent on é.

3. SPEAK IN COMPLETE SENTENCES
Je regarde la télévision. = I watch television.
J’écoute la musique. = I listen to the music being discussed.
J’aime le fromage. = I like cheese.
Regarder and écouter do not need an extra à before the thing: « J’écoute la musique », NOT « J’écoute à la musique ».
Later we will learn « écouter de la musique » to mean listening to music in general; you do not need that new grammar today.

4. TODAY'S FIVE FOOD WORDS
le riz (rice), le poisson (fish), les légumes (vegetables), les fruits (fruit), le fromage (cheese).
Try them with aimer: J’aime le riz. / Elle aime le poisson. / Nous aimons les légumes.
Notice: les légumes and les fruits are plural.

5. CHECK THE VERB ENDING
vous regardez (not vous regardons)
elles écoutent (not elles écoute)
j’écoute (not je écoute)

6. TRY FROM MEMORY
Say: “We watch television.” → Nous regardons la télévision.
Say: “I like the vegetables.” → J’aime les légumes.
Close the notes and respond aloud before typing.
fixed: Je regarde la télévision. — I watch television.
J’écoute la musique. — I listen to music.
J’aime le riz. — I like rice. (old verb)

recall.explanation: Riz is masculine: le riz (final z is normally silent).
Poisson is masculine: le poisson.
Légumes is plural: les légumes, with é.
Fruits is plural: les fruits.
Fromage is masculine: le fromage.
Pain from Day 3 is masculine: le pain.
Chercher with nous takes -ons: nous cherchons.

drills.explanation: Before écouter, je becomes j’: j’écoute; keep é.
Regarder with vous ends -ez: vous regardez.
Écouter with nous ends -ons: nous écoutons.
Regarder with elles ends -ent: elles regardent.
Recall chercher with tu: tu cherches (-es).

sentences.explanation: Je regarde la télévision: direct object, no preposition after regarder.

sentences.prompt: We listen to the music (a particular piece of music).
sentences.explanation: Nous écoutons la musique refers to the music being discussed; écouter takes a direct object.
Elle aime le poisson: French uses the definite article after aimer for general likes.

changes.prompt: Je regarde les fruits. → Change je to elles.
changes.explanation: Je regarde → elles regardent; les fruits stays plural.

changes.prompt: Tu écoutes la musique. → Change tu to nous.
changes.explanation: Tu écoutes → nous écoutons; keep the accent on écouter.

oral: Tu aimes le fromage ou le poisson ?
Say in French: We watch television.
Say in French: She likes fish.
Say in French, recalling Day 3: They are looking for the bread.
exit: Write a NEW sentence using regarder.
Nous regardons la télévision.
Write a NEW sentence using écouter.
Elle écoute la musique.

days.title: Construire des phrases — 8 verbes
days.focus: Combine all eight -ER verbs into accurate, short everyday statements and answers.
days.yesterday: Review Day 4: regarder, écouter, riz, poisson, légumes, fruits, fromage. Recycle older verbs on purpose.
days.explanation:
DAY 5 — SIMPLE NOTES: BUILD LONGER SENTENCES

1. TODAY IS A PRACTICE DAY
No new verbs and no new vocabulary. Reuse all eight verbs:
parler (speak), travailler (work), habiter (live), aimer (like), chercher (look for), demander (ask for), regarder (watch), écouter (listen to).

2. BUILD A SENTENCE IN THREE SMALL STEPS
Step A: Choose WHO. → Je / Tu / Elle / Nous / Vous / Ils.
Step B: Choose the correct VERB. → Nous habitons.
Step C: Add WHERE or WHAT. → Nous habitons dans une maison.

3. MAKE TWO IDEAS INTO ONE
Use et (= and) to join two easy ideas:
J’habite dans un appartement. J’aime le salon.
→ J’habite dans un appartement et j’aime le salon.
One correct, longer sentence is better than several guessed words.

4. KEEP THREE IMPORTANT RULES
With nous, use -ons: nous parlons / nous regardons.
With vous, use -ez: vous travaillez / vous écoutez.
With ils/elles, use -ent: ils cherchent / elles aiment.
Use j’ in j’habite, j’aime and j’écoute.

5. FIX COMMON ERRORS
NOT « Je parle de français » when you mean I speak French → Je parle français.
NOT « Je cherche pour le livre » → Je cherche le livre.
NOT « une appartement » → un appartement.

6. SPEAK WITHOUT NOTES
Say two sentences: where you live and what you like.
Model: J’habite dans une maison. J’aime la cuisine.
Then try the mixed exercises. If a mistake repeats, practise that exact pattern again.
fixed: J’habite dans un appartement et je travaille à la maison. — I live in an apartment and work at home.
Elle regarde la télévision et j’écoute la musique. — She watches television and I listen to the music.
Elle aime les fruits. — She likes fruit.

recall.explanation: Fenêtre is feminine, and ê takes a circumflex.
Pain is masculine: le pain.
Fromage is masculine: le fromage.
Supermarché is masculine; the é accent matters.
Je shortens to j’ before écouter; keep é.
Ils takes the -ent ending on regular -ER verbs.

drills.explanation: The regular -ER ending for nous is -ons.
With tu, a regular -ER verb ends in -es.
Elles requires -ent for a regular -ER verb.
Je becomes j’ before aimer, with an -e ending.
Vous takes -ez, and écouter keeps its accent.
Il uses -e for regular -ER verbs.

sentences.prompt: I live in an apartment and I like the kitchen.
sentences.answer: J’habite dans un appartement et j’aime la cuisine.
sentences.explanation: Both j’habite and j’aime use elision; la cuisine is feminine.

sentences.prompt: We are looking for the book.
sentences.explanation: Nous takes -ons and chercher takes a direct object (no pour).
Elle takes -e; the everyday fixed expression is à la maison.
Ils/elles takes -ent; télévision is feminine.

changes.prompt: Je parle français. → Change je to vous.
changes.explanation: Vous uses -ez and does not add any preposition after parler français.

changes.prompt: Nous aimons le poisson. → Change nous to elle.
changes.explanation: Elle takes -e; le poisson stays masculine.

changes.prompt: Elle écoute la musique. → Change elle to ils.
changes.explanation: Ils takes -ent, usually silent.

changes.prompt: Tu habites dans une maison. → Change tu to nous.
changes.explanation: Nous takes -ons; une maison is feminine.

oral: Tu habites dans une maison ou dans un appartement ?
Tu regardes la télévision à la maison ?
Oui, je regarde la télévision à la maison.
Say in French: They are looking for the book.
Say in French: We work at home.
Say in French: I listen to the music.
Speak two different sentences: where you live and what you like.
J’habite dans une maison. J’aime la cuisine.
Ask your teacher in French: Do you speak French?
exit: Write one NEW sentence using chercher and a noun with an article.
Je cherche la chaise.
Write one NEW sentence using a plural subject and écouter.
Ils écoutent la musique.
Write TWO sentences about where you live and what you like.
J’habite dans un appartement. J’aime le salon.

days.title: Test diagnostique — mémoire active
days.focus: Identify weak verbs, noun articles and sentence order in a closed-notes practice test.
days.yesterday: Recall Day 5 mixed practice. Do the first attempt without model answers or conjugation tables.
days.explanation:
DAY 6 — SIMPLE NOTES: REVIEW AND FIND YOUR WEAK POINTS

1. TODAY IS A CHECK-UP, NOT A NEW LESSON
No new verbs, vocabulary or grammar. We want to see what you can remember WITHOUT notes.

2. FIRST, TRY IT ALONE
Say or write these from memory:
I speak → je parle. | We work → nous travaillons.
I live → j’habite. | They look for → ils cherchent.
Then test the nouns with their articles: la chambre, le fromage, les œufs.

3. IF YOU GET STUCK, ASK THREE QUESTIONS
WHO is doing it? (je, tu, il, nous...)
Which ENDING do I need? (-e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent)
Which ARTICLE belongs to the noun? (le, la, l’, les, un or une)
Try again BEFORE looking at the model answer.

4. SPEAK, THEN CORRECT
First, say the sentence aloud. Next, compare it with the model. Finally, repeat the corrected sentence twice without looking.
Example: NOT « Nous travaille » → « Nous travaillons. » Repeat: Nous travaillons à la maison.

5. PUT MISTAKES IN FOUR GROUPS
Verb endings: tu parles / nous parlons.
Articles and gender: la chaise / le salon.
Apostrophe and accents: j’aime / j’écoute / l’épicerie.
Sentence order: Je cherche le livre (not Je cherche pour le livre).

6. YOUR GOAL
Find your two weakest patterns today. Correct each one in three new sentences. Tomorrow you will use the same vocabulary to learn article rules.
fixed: Je cherche la fenêtre. — I am looking for the window.
Ils travaillent à la maison. — They work at home.
Nous aimons le poisson. — We like fish.

recall.explanation: Chambre is feminine: la chambre.
Chaise is feminine: la chaise.
Supermarché is masculine and takes é.
Œufs is plural here; use les.
Fromage is masculine: le fromage.
Elide je before aimer, and write -e.
Nous needs the -ons ending.
Elles requires -ent, and écouter has é.

drills.explanation: Ils takes -ent; no final -s on the verb.
Nous takes -ons.
Je elides before the silent h of habiter.
Vous takes -ez.
Tu takes -es.
Elle takes -e.
Nous takes -ons; keep é.
Je takes -e; chercher does not need pour before a direct object.

sentences.explanation: Ils/elles takes -ent; à la maison means at home.
Elle uses the -e ending; maison is feminine so une.
Aimer with nous takes -ons; les légumes is plural.

sentences.prompt: I am looking for the door.
sentences.explanation: Chercher takes a direct object; porte is feminine.
Vous takes -ez; no preposition after regarder.

changes.prompt: Je parle français. → Change je to elles.
changes.explanation: Elles takes -ent and parler français needs no preposition.

changes.prompt: Nous cherchons la chaise. → Change nous to tu.
changes.explanation: Tu needs -es.

changes.prompt: Il aime le riz. → Change il to nous.
changes.explanation: Nous takes -ons.

changes.prompt: Tu écoutes la musique. → Change tu to je.
changes.explanation: Use j’ before écouter; je écoute is incorrect.

Say in French: We like the house.
Say in French: They listen to the music.
Tu aimes le poisson ou les légumes ?
Say in French: She works at home.
Ask the teacher in French: Do you watch television?

days.title: Articles, genre et pluriel — bilan
days.focus: Choose definite and indefinite articles accurately, use plural nouns and demonstrate independent Week 1 speaking.
days.yesterday: Review Day 6 errors first: verb endings, gender/articles, j’ before a vowel, and noun accents.
days.explanation:
DAY 7 — SIMPLE GRAMMAR NOTES: ARTICLES, GENDER AND PLURAL

1. WHAT IS AN ARTICLE?
An article is a small word placed before a noun (a person, place or thing).
English examples: THE house; A chair; SOME chairs.
French examples: LA maison; UNE chaise; DES chaises.
The article helps us understand what kind of thing we mean.

2. EVERY FRENCH NOUN HAS A GRAMMATICAL GENDER
Masculine examples: le salon, le livre, le fromage, l’appartement.
Feminine examples: la maison, la chaise, la cuisine, l’épicerie.
This is the gender of the FRENCH WORD, not the gender of a person.
Important: learn the article together with each new noun. Do not guess from the English word.

3. USE LE / LA / L’ / LES WHEN YOU MEAN “THE”
LE = the + masculine singular → le salon (the living room).
LA = the + feminine singular → la maison (the house).
L’ = the + singular word starting with a vowel sound → l’appartement; l’épicerie.
LES = the + plural noun → les chaises; les œufs.
The apostrophe in l’ takes the place of le or la; it does not change the noun's gender.

4. USE UN / UNE / DES WHEN YOU MEAN “A / AN / SOME”
UN = a/an + masculine singular → un salon; un appartement.
UNE = a/an + feminine singular → une maison; une épicerie.
DES = some + plural countable things → des chaises; des œufs.
Notice: We say l’appartement but UN appartement. We say l’épicerie but UNE épicerie.

5. WHAT DOES SINGULAR OR PLURAL MEAN?
Singular = ONE thing: une chaise, le livre.
Plural = TWO OR MORE things: des chaises, les livres.
For many nouns, add -s to the noun when it becomes plural:
une chaise → des chaises
le livre → les livres
la maison → les maisons
Also change the article. Do not write « des chaise ».

6. HOW DO I CHOOSE THE RIGHT ARTICLE?
Ask yourself these questions in order:
A. One thing or many things? → singular or plural.
B. Do I mean “the” specific thing or “a/some” nonspecific things?
C. If singular, is the French noun masculine or feminine?
D. If I need le/la before a vowel sound, change it to l’.
Example: “I am looking for a chair.” → any one chair → une chaise.
Example: “I am looking for the chair.” → a particular chair → la chaise.
Example: “I am looking for some chairs.” → more than one, not specified → des chaises.

7. ONE USEFUL EXTRA RULE WITH AIMER
To talk about food or things you like IN GENERAL, use le/la/les:
J’aime le fromage. = I like cheese.
J’aime les légumes. = I like vegetables.
You do not need to learn du/de la food expressions today. Those come later.

8. COMMON MISTAKES TO FIX
NOT « le maison » → la maison.
NOT « une appartement » → un appartement.
NOT « le épicerie » → l’épicerie.
NOT « des chaise » → des chaises.
NOT « les livre » → les livres.

9. YOUR QUICK PRACTICE BEFORE THE TEST
A. The house → la maison. A house → une maison.
B. The apartment → l’appartement. An apartment → un appartement.
C. A chair → une chaise. Some chairs → des chaises.
D. Change to plural: Je cherche une chaise. → Je cherche des chaises.
Now hide these notes and complete the Week 1 final assessment without looking.
fixed: Je cherche la maison. / Je cherche une maison. — I am looking for the house. / I am looking for a house.
J’habite dans un appartement. — I live in an apartment.
Je cherche des chaises. — I am looking for some chairs.
J’aime les légumes. — I like vegetables.
flashcards: I am looking for the door

recall.explanation: Maison is feminine; the definite article is la.
A singular indefinite feminine noun takes une.
Appartement is masculine; le elides to l’ before a vowel.
Appartement is masculine even though the definite article is l’.
Épicerie is feminine; la elides to l’.
Épicerie is feminine: une épicerie.
The definite plural article is les.
Indefinite plural countable nouns take des.

drills.explanation: Before the silent h in habiter, use j’; ending -e.
Vous takes -ez.
Elles takes -ent.
Nous takes -ons.
Tu takes -es; keep é.
Il takes -e.

sentences.explanation: Habiter with je becomes j’habite; maison is feminine so une.
Use l’ before the vowel and aimer + definite article.

sentences.prompt: We are looking for a supermarket.
sentences.explanation: Supermarché is masculine; un shows one non-specific supermarket.
Aimer + plural definite article: les; ils/elles takes -ent.

sentences.prompt: She is looking for a chair.
sentences.explanation: Chaise is feminine: une chaise.
Nous takes -ons; télévision takes la in this expression.

changes.prompt: Je cherche une chaise. → Change to more than one chair.
changes.explanation: Une → des in the indefinite plural; chaise normally adds -s.

changes.prompt: Il regarde le livre. → Change the book to the books.
changes.explanation: Le → les and livre adds -s.

changes.prompt: Nous aimons la chambre. → Change the bedroom to the bedrooms.
changes.explanation: La → les and chambre adds -s.

changes.prompt: J’habite dans un appartement. → Replace appartement with maison.
changes.explanation: Maison is feminine, so use une rather than un.

changes.prompt: Je cherche le salon. → Replace salon with appartement.
changes.explanation: The masculine definite le elides to l’ before appartement.

oral: Say in French: I live in an apartment.
Say in French: We are looking for a chair.

Say in French and make plural: I am looking for some windows.
Tu habites dans une maison ou dans un appartement ?
Tu aimes les fruits ou le fromage ?

Produce TWO sentences: one about your home, one about something you like.

exit: Write a NEW sentence with une + a familiar noun.
Je cherche une chaise.
Write a NEW sentence with les + a familiar plural noun.
J’aime les légumes.
Write two sentences using habiter and aimer; choose the articles carefully.
J’habite dans un appartement. J’aime la cuisine.
